question.text:
The table below defines the function $f(x).$ Is the function even, odd, or neither?

$x$ $-6$ $-4$ $-2$ $2$ $4$ $6$
$f(x)$ $85$ $75$ $30$ $-30$ $-75$ $-85$
question.explanation:
Recall that

  • a function is even if $f(-x) = f(x)$ for all $x$ in the domain of $f$

  • a function is odd if $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for all $x$ in the domain of $f$

For our function, we have

\begin{align*} f(-6) &= 85 = -f(6) , \\[3pt] f(-4) &= 75 = -f(4) , \\[3pt] f(-2) &= 30 = -f(2) . \end{align*}

This means that $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for all $x$ in the domain of the function. Therefore, $f(x)$ is an odd function.

question.text: Is the function $f(x)=x^3+8x$ even, odd, or neither?
question.explanation:
Recall that

  • a function is even if $f(-x) = f(x)$ for all $x$

  • a function is odd if $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for all $x$

Computing $f(-x)$ for the given function and comparing it to $f(x),$ we have

\begin{align} f(-x) &= (-x)^3+8(-x)\\[3pt] &=-x^3-8x. \end{align}

Since $f(-x) \neq f(x),$ the function is not even.

Lastly, we compute $-f(x)$ and get \begin{align} -f(x) &= -(x^3+8x) \\[3pt] &= -x^3-8x. \end{align}

Since $f(-x)= -f(x),$ the function is odd.

example.title: Classifying Even and Odd Functions Using the Algebraic Definition

question.text: Which of the above could be graphs of odd functions?
question.explanation:
Recall that the graph of an odd function must have rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin.

  • Graphs II, III, and IV do not have rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. So, it is not an odd function.

  • On the other hand, graph I does have rotational symmetry about the origin. If we rotate the graph $180^\circ$ around the origin, we get the same picture. This means that graph I show odd functions.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
